bib.title: Bandit Algorithms, Chapter 9: The Upper Confidence Bound Algorithm: Minimax Optimality

question: Can the log(n) factor in the worst-case regret of UCB be removed, and what does that cost?
contributions: MOSS algorithm (Alg. 7) with regret <= 39 sqrt(kn) + sum Delta_i
Two drawbacks of MOSS: worse than UCB on some instances; unstable regret distribution

results.claim: MOSS worst-case regret bound has constant 39 on sqrt(kn) (Theorem 9.1), removing the log factor
results.setup: Any 1-subgaussian k-armed stochastic bandit, horizon n known; MOSS index mu_hat_i + sqrt(4/T_i log+(n/(k T_i)))
results.quote: Theorem 9.1. For any 1-subgaussian bandit, the regret of Algorithm 7 satisﬁes

results.setup: Proof of Thm 9.1, via Lemma 9.3 and Prop 2.8

results.claim: Lemma 9.3 tail bound constant 15 delta / Delta^2
results.setup: Independent 1-subgaussian, delta in (0,1), any Delta>0; peeling over geometric grid [2^j,2^(j+1)]

results.claim: Per-arm term: Delta_i E[kappa_i] <= Delta_i + 15 sqrt(n/k) for Delta_i >= 8 sqrt(k/n)
Theorem 9.2 (maximal inequality) P(exists t<=n: S_t>=eps) <= exp(-eps^2/(2 n sigma^2)), via Doob's submartingale inequality
Counterexample: UCB regret O(k log k) but MOSS Omega(sqrt(kn)) = Omega(k^2)
results.setup: Gaussian unit-variance rewards, n=k^3, mu_1=0, mu_2=-sqrt(k/n), mu_i=-1 for i>2; proof described as delicate and not given

results.claim: Instability: tuning delta=1/(n Delta^2) gives second moment of failure regret Omega(n); delta=(n Delta)^-2 gives O(1) at slight regret cost
results.setup: Two-armed Gaussian bandit, gap Delta, bimodal regret heuristic (informal)

results.claim: MOSS asymptotically: limsup R_n/log n <= sum 4/Delta_i; modified MOSS (2 in place of 4) attains optimal sum 2/Delta_i
results.setup: Note 1; proof not given, refers to Garivier 2013

results.claim: Instance-dependent bound for MOSS is left as Exercise 9.2: R_n <= C k/Delta_min log+(n Delta_min^2/k) + sum Delta_i, universal C
results.setup: Exercise, not proven in chapter; Delta_min = min over Delta_i>0

results.claim: Less aggressive index with log+(n/T_i) is never worse than UCB and has distribution-free regret O(sqrt(nk log k)) (Exercise 9.3)
results.setup: Note 2; Exercise 9.3 asks for proof, also R_n<=C sum (Delta_i+ log+(n Delta_i^2)/Delta_i)

limits: MOSS needs the horizon n (anytime variant by Degenne and Perchet 2016 in notes).
MOSS can be arbitrarily worse than UCB on some instances (n=k^3 counterexample); the Omega(k^2) claim is not proved in the chapter.
Minimax lower bound deferred to Part IV; instance-dependent bound is only an exercise.
No simulations or experiments in the chapter; only exercise 9.4(i) asks for an empirical comparison.
practices: Choose the confidence level from per-arm plays, n and k (Alg. 7) to drop the log factor from the minimax bound (Sec 9.1).
To mitigate MOSS instability use the less aggressive index mu_hat + sqrt(4/T_i log+(n/T_i)) (Eq. 9.2, Note 2).
Use adaptive confidence levels (optimally confident UCB, AdaUCB) to be minimax optimal and never worse than UCB (Note 3).
Prefer delta=(n Delta)^-2 over 1/(n Delta^2) when the second moment of regret matters (Sec 9.2).

terms.definition: the directly named 'minimax optimal strategy in the stochastic case' algorithm
union bound over a geometric grid of intervals [2^j, 2^(j+1)] to prove time-uniform bounds; also used for the law of the iterated logarithm
